questions.text: The Floyd-Warshall algorithm for all-pair shortest paths computation is based on
questions.solution:
Floyd-Warshall builds [latex]d_k[i][j]=\min(d_{k-1}[i][j],\ d_{k-1}[i][k]+d_{k-1}[k][j])[/latex], reusing answers of smaller subproblems. That is dynamic programming.

Answer: Dynamic Programming paradigm

questions.text:
Assume that the algorithms considered here sort the input sequences in ascending order. If the input is already in ascending order, which of the following are TRUE?
I. Quicksort runs in [latex]\Theta (n^{2})[/latex] time
II. Bubblesort runs in [latex]\Theta (n^{2})[/latex] time
III. Merge sort runs in [latex]\Theta (n)[/latex] time
IV. Insertion sort runs in [latex]\Theta (n)[/latex] time
questions.solution:
On already sorted input:
- Quicksort (first/last element as pivot) makes the most unbalanced splits [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]\Theta(n^2)[/latex] True
- Bubble sort with the "no swap" check stops after one pass [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]\Theta(n)[/latex] False
- Merge sort is always [latex]\Theta(n\log n)[/latex] False
- Insertion sort compares each element once [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]\Theta(n)[/latex] True

Answer: I and IV only

questions.text: Breadth First Search(BFS) is started on a binary tree beginning from the root vertex. There is a vertex t at a distance four from the root. If t is the n-th vertex in this BFS traversal, then the maximum possible value of n is______ .
questions.solution:
BFS visits level by level. To make t as late as possible, levels 0-3 are full (1 + 2 + 4 + 8 = 15 nodes) and t is the last of the 16 nodes at level 4.

n = 15 + 16 = 31

Answer: 31

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.text:
G = (V,E) is an undirected simple graph in which each edge has a distinct weight,and e is a particular edgeof G. Which of the following statements about the minimum spanning trees (MSTs) of G is/are TRUE?
I. If e is the lightest edge of some cycle in G, then every MST of G includes e
II. If e is the heaviest edge of some cycle in G, then every MST of G excludes e
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: the lightest edge of one cycle can still be the heaviest edge of another cycle and be excluded [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- II: cycle property: with distinct weights, the heaviest edge of any cycle is in no MST [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.

Answer: II only

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.text: Let G be a complete undirected graph on 4 vertices, having 6 edges  with weights being 1,2,3,4,5, and 6. The maximum possible weight that a minimum weight spanning tree of G can haveis .
questions.solution:
An MST of 4 vertices has 3 edges; edges 1 and 2 are always taken (two edges cannot form a cycle).

To make the third edge as heavy as possible, put edges 1, 2, 3 in a triangle, so 3 is rejected. The 4th vertex must then be joined by the next lightest edge, 4.

Maximum MST weight = 1 + 2 + 4 = 7

Answer: 7
